MUTUAL NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of January 11, 2021 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Meridian Mechanical Group, Inc., a business entity organized and existing under applicable law ("Meridian"), and FieldFlow Software, Inc., a business entity organized and existing under applicable law ("Counterparty"). Meridian and Counterparty are collectively referred to herein as the "Parties" and individually as a "Party."

WHEREAS, Meridian and Counterparty desire to explore a business opportunity of mutual interest, which may involve the furnishing of information by one Party to the other with respect to evaluation of field-service management software (the "Purpose"); and

WHEREAS, in connection with their discussion and evaluation of the Purpose, each Party may disclose to the other Party certain confidential and proprietary information; and

WHEREAS, the Parties desire to protect the confidentiality of such information and to establish the terms and conditions under which such information shall be disclosed and used.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

SECTION 1. PURPOSE.

The Parties acknowledge that they are entering into this Agreement in order to evaluate and explore a potential business relationship with respect to evaluation of field-service management software. The Parties intend to exchange certain information with each other to facilitate this evaluation and exploration. Nothing in this Agreement obligates either Party to proceed with any transaction, arrangement, or business relationship, and nothing herein constitutes an offer to buy or sell any product or service.

SECTION 2. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION.

(a) Definition. "Confidential Information" means all information, whether in written, oral, electronic, or any other form, disclosed by one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") in connection with the Purpose, including but not limited to: technical data, trade secrets, know-how, research, product plans, specifications, designs, drawings, customer lists, supplier lists, pricing information, cost information, business plans, financial information, marketing strategies, contracts, manufacturing processes, formulations, methods, techniques, equipment specifications, and any other proprietary or non-public information related to the business, operations, products, services, or financial condition of the Disclosing Party. Confidential Information shall include all notes, analyses, compilations, or derivative works created by the Receiving Party that contain or reflect the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

(b) Exclusions from Confidential Information. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following shall not be considered Confidential Information under this Agreement:

(i) Information that is or becomes publicly available through no breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party;

(ii) Information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written record was lawfully in its possession prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party;

(iii) Information that the Receiving Party rightfully receives from a third party without breach of any confidentiality obligation, as evidenced by written record;

(iv) Information that is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reliance upon the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by written record;

(v) Information that is required to be disclosed by law, regulation, court order, or governmental authority, provided that the Receiving Party provides prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party and cooperates in any efforts by the Disclosing Party to seek protective measures; and

(vi) General ideas, concepts, or know-how retained in the unaided memory of the Receiving Party's employees, provided that such knowledge is not combined with or derived from the Confidential Information.

SECTION 3. RECEIVING PARTY OBLIGATIONS.

(a) Duty of Confidentiality. The Receiving Party agrees to:

(i) Maintain the confidentiality of all Confidential Information received from the Disclosing Party and to protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential and proprietary information of similar nature, but in no event less than reasonable care;

(ii) Restrict access to the Confidential Information to employees, agents, representatives, advisors, and contractors of the Receiving Party who have a legitimate business need to know such information in connection with the Purpose and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those contained in this Agreement;

(iii) Not use the Confidential Information for any purpose other than evaluation of the Purpose and the potential business relationship, unless otherwise authorized in writing by the Disclosing Party;

(iv) Not disclose the Confidential Information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party, except as permitted under Section 4 of this Agreement.

(b) Limited Use. The Receiving Party shall use the Confidential Information solely for purposes of evaluating whether to proceed with the contemplated business relationship with respect to the Purpose. The Receiving Party shall not use the Confidential Information to compete with, gain unfair advantage over, or develop products or services in competition with the Disclosing Party.

(c) No Reverse Engineering. The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer, disassemble, decompile, or otherwise attempt to derive the underlying information or trade secrets from any materials provided by the Disclosing Party, except to the extent such activity is permitted by law and then only with the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party.

SECTION 4. PERMITTED DISCLOSURES.

The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information in the following limited circumstances, provided that the Receiving Party takes reasonable steps to ensure that the recipient is bound by confidentiality obligations:

(a) To the Receiving Party's employees, agents, representatives, and contractors who have a need to know the information in connection with the Purpose and who are subject to written confidentiality obligations at least as restrictive as this Agreement;

(b) To the Receiving Party's legal, financial, and accounting advisors who are providing services with respect to the evaluation of the Purpose and who are subject to professional duties of confidentiality;

(c) As required by applicable law, regulation, court order, regulatory inquiry, or other governmental process, provided that the Receiving Party promptly notifies the Disclosing Party of such requirement and cooperates in any reasonable efforts by the Disclosing Party to obtain protective measures.

SECTION 5. TERM.

(a) Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon written notice, shall continue in full force and effect for a period of three (3) years, after which the confidentiality obligations set forth herein shall terminate and be of no further force or effect (the "Term").

(b) Survival. Notwithstanding the expiration of the Term, the Receiving Party's obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall survive termination of this Agreement and continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret under applicable law.

SECTION 6. RETURN OF MATERIALS.

(a) Return or Destruction. Upon request by the Disclosing Party, or upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall, at the Disclosing Party's election: (i) promptly return to the Disclosing Party all tangible materials containing or representing Confidential Information; or (ii) destroy all such tangible materials in a manner that prevents recovery or use of the information contained therein.

(b) Certification. The Receiving Party shall provide written certification to the Disclosing Party, signed by an authorized officer, certifying that all requested materials have been returned or destroyed in accordance with subsection (a) above, within thirty (30) days of the Disclosing Party's request or termination of this Agreement.

(c) Exception. The Receiving Party may retain one archival copy of Confidential Information in its legal files for record-keeping purposes and may retain copies as required by law, provided that such retained copies shall remain subject to all confidentiality obligations contained herein.

SECTION 7. NO LICENSE OR OBLIGATION.

(a) No License. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting any license, right, or interest in any Confidential Information or any intellectual property rights of the Disclosing Party. All Confidential Information is provided on an "as is" basis without warranty of any kind, express or implied.

(b) No Obligation to Disclose. Nothing in this Agreement obligates either Party to disclose any particular information, to enter into any business relationship or transaction, or to furnish any specific data or details. Each Party retains the right, in its sole discretion, to determine what information it will disclose.

(c) No Obligation to Negotiate. This Agreement does not create any obligation on either Party to negotiate, enter into, or complete any transaction or business relationship.

SECTION 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS.

All intellectual property rights, including without limitation patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, and know-how contained in or relating to the Confidential Information remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party. The Receiving Party acknowledges the proprietary nature of the Confidential Information and agrees not to challenge or contest the validity or ownership of any intellectual property rights of the Disclosing Party.

SECTION 9. DTSA IMMUNITY NOTICE.

(a) Immunity Notice. Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. Section 1833(b), the Receiving Party is notified that: An individual may not be held criminally or civilly liable under any Federal or State trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made (1) in confidence to a Federal, State, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney, and solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (2) in a complaint or filing under seal in a lawsuit or other proceeding. An individual may also not be held criminally or civilly liable under any Federal or State trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made in good faith in a complaint or filing made in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. Furthermore, pursuant to 18 U.S.C. Section 1833(b), if an individual is unable to obtain such seal, the individual may file the complaint or other document without obtaining such seal and still be protected from liability, provided that an individual files any document containing trade secrets under seal and does not disclose the trade secrets except pursuant to court order.

(b) Construction. Nothing in this Agreement is intended to prohibit disclosure of Confidential Information in accordance with the protections afforded under 18 U.S.C. Section 1833(b).

SECTION 10. RESIDUAL KNOWLEDGE.

The Receiving Party acknowledges that its employees may develop or retain general knowledge, skills, experience, and know-how during the course of performing their duties. Notwithstanding the confidentiality obligations hereunder, the Receiving Party shall have the right to use general ideas, concepts, or know-how retained in the unaided memory of its employees that do not contain, reflect, or incorporate any specific Confidential Information, provided that such residual knowledge is not combined with or derived from the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

SECTION 11. REMEDIES.

The Receiving Party acknowledges that any breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. In addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief to prevent any breach or threatened breach of this Agreement without the necessity of posting bond or proving actual damages.

SECTION 12. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION.

(a) Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

(b) Jurisdiction and Venue. Each Party hereby consents to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in the State of California for resolution of any disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement.

SECTION 13. MISCELLANEOUS.

(a) Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter.

(b) Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

(c) Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect to the maximum extent permitted by law.

(d) Waiver. No waiver of any provision or breach of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by an authorized representative of the Party against whom the waiver is sought. Waiver of any breach shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach.

(e) Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Electronic signatures and PDF signatures shall be deemed original signatures.

(f) Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, consolidation, or sale of substantially all assets, provided that any such assignee agrees to be bound by the terms hereof.

(g) Equitable Relief. Each Party acknowledges that breaches of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm not adequately compensable by monetary damages, and each Party is entitled to equitable relief, including specific performance and injunctive relief, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity.

(h) Notices. All notices required under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be delivered personally, by overnight courier, by certified mail (return receipt requested), or by electronic mail (with confirmation of receipt), to the addresses set forth below, or to such other addresses as either Party may designate by written notice to the other.

(i) Independent Contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency, or employment relationship between the Parties. Each Party is an independent contractor.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Mutual Nondisclosure Agreement as of the Effective Date.
